<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a73edb3cd784e212c7b8b21757a44c0cfed9adfe`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a73edb3cd784e212c7b8b21757a44c0cfed9adfe` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9390ea1d5cb516fe324c6e6653b1d8bc4911cd86` — the merge of head `8ef5a6dd11a5f666c711162009c7ad17bb5350a9` into base `a73edb3cd784e212c7b8b21757a44c0cfed9adfe`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9390ea1d5cb516fe324c6e6653b1d8bc4911cd86 && git checkout 9390ea1d5cb516fe324c6e6653b1d8bc4911cd86
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a73edb3cd784e212c7b8b21757a44c0cfed9adfe 8ef5a6dd11a5f666c711162009c7ad17bb5350a9 && git checkout -B drift-repro a73edb3cd784e212c7b8b21757a44c0cfed9adfe && git merge --no-ff 8ef5a6dd11a5f666c711162009c7ad17bb5350a9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a73edb3cd784e212c7b8b21757a44c0cfed9adfe
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a73edb3cd784e212c7b8b21757a44c0cfed9adfe` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · head 8ef5a6dd11a5f666c711162009c7ad17bb5350a9

2026-11-24T16:24Z · L1 (one-shot reviewer), checked against GitHub and `origin/main` (merge base `57445a69981`), not against the report's own account. Card #36052, scope widening 7063882080, claim 7112268942 plus amendments 7129930826 and 7132980427, dev report 7136639661.

**CI on this head:** all check-runs completed at 2026-11-24T16:24Z: 57 `success` and 11 `skipped`, with 0 failed, 0 cancelled and 0 pending. The required floor is green: `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are `success`. `Build Core` (which runs `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure`), `Type Check · debt ledger` (which runs `check:type-check-debt`) and `Check Changeset` are also `success`. `.changeset/36050-view-all-fields-bit.md` is still pending on `origin/main` at the time of this record.

### Checklist

1. **PR shape:** draft, base `main`. Line 1 is the seat signature and line 3 is `Fixes #36052`. The signature-first opener is the fleet's rule (every first-line recogniser skips one leading signature line), so this is not a deviation. `Fixes` is right: both legs of the card are delivered, the cross-set warning and the widened `security-wildcard-vama`. I scanned the whole body: no closing keyword sits next to another open card number (#34365 is cited without a verb).
2. **Scope:** 8 files, +732/−18, all in `packages/lint` plus one changeset. Nothing under `content/docs/releases/`, and no codegen script in the head diff.
   - `packages/lint/src/index.ts` (+1, the `SECURITY_CROSS_SET_FIELD_REOPEN` export) is outside the claim's file surface. **Accepted.** It is part of this deliverable, not a fix to a neighbouring defect. Every sibling rule id is re-exported from the same barrel (for example `SECURITY_SUPERUSER_FIELD_MASK_INERT` at :414), and the PR body names the file. The claim surface was not amended to list it (amendment 3 says "unchanged"). That is a record gap, not REWORK.
3. **Changeset:** `@objectstack/lint` `patch`, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in both the body and the changeset. I checked each sentence of `.changeset/36052-cross-set-field-reopen.md` against the diff:
   - "hides a field (`readable: false`) or makes it read-only": the diff tests `readable === false` and `editable !== true`.
   - "own entry for the object, or its `'*'` entry when it has none": `objects[o] || objects['*']`, a lookup, never a merge.
   - "own `readable: false` row … works beside View All and View All Fields, not beside Modify All": `ownRow` is emitted only when `!vote.editable`.
   - "say `viewAllFields: true`": the code omits this when the bit is already `viewAllFields`.
   - The `requiredPermissions` + `maskingRule` steering matches.
   - Each "Not reported" item maps to a `continue` in `pushCrossSetFieldReopen`: capability-gated fields, the hiding set's own Modify All, the second set's own read mask, an edit lock beside View All or `viewAllFields`, and an undeclared object or field.
   - The wildcard paragraph matches the `security-wildcard-vama` hunk.
   - All sentences are true.
4. **Vote reading against core:** lint's `holdsViewAllFields` and `objectWideFieldVote` match `@objectstack/core`'s `holdsViewAllFields`, `superuserFieldVote` and `declaresOwnReadMask` on `origin/main` line by line: Modify All votes read and edit, View All and `viewAllFields` vote read only, and a set's own `readable: false` beats them.
   - **The copied helper is accepted** as noted. `@objectstack/lint` does not depend on core, and `holdsSuperuserBypass` is already the same kind of copy. Neither needs a card now.
5. **Tests:** the five acceptance fixtures on the card map to cases in `validate-security-posture-cross-set-field-reopen-36052.test.ts`:
   - View All fires.
   - Modify All fires, as `both`.
   - `viewAllFields` fires, on the object's own entry and through `'*'`.
   - One set alone does not fire.
   - A `requiredPermissions` field does not fire.
   - Also covered: no double report with `security-superuser-field-mask-inert` (one row, one rule), and three wildcard cases.
   - The ablation shows the guards can fail: removing the call gives 6/16 red, and `fieldBypass` → `false` gives 2/16 red, each restored to the HEAD blob.
6. **Local NOT MEASURED** (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:type-check-debt`): **accepted**. Each has a stated cause, and the seat's evidence is the check-runs on this head, not the local subset. Build Core and the Type Check jobs that run these three are covered by the CI line above.

### The `viewAllFields`-as-error leg: is it an undeclared narrowing?

**No.** The card's declaration note ("a warning; nothing an author writes is refused") was written before the scope widening. The widening (7063882080) left error versus warning open for the PR to decide, and the PR body and changeset both say error and why.

It refuses nothing a published version accepted. The released `@objectstack/spec@18.6.0` `ObjectPermissionSchema` is `.strict()` and has no `viewAllFields` key, so every released version already refused `objects['*']: { viewAllFields: true }`. The key arrives with `.changeset/36050-view-all-fields-bit.md` (`Metadata-protocol: added`), which is still pending on `origin/main`. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` therefore hold for this PR.

**Landing condition:** if a release consumes `.changeset/36050-view-all-fields-bit.md` before this PR merges, the error leg becomes a narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` / `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`), and this PR must re-declare before it lands. Check again just before arming.

### Effort size

**M holds.** The diff is +732/−18 over 8 files, with a design judgement inside it: error versus warning, and the double-report boundary with the same-set rule. Under 定档 that is M → default judgement tier, effort `high`, which matches amendment 2 (7129930826). There is no MANDATORY `--tier` path (lint only), so the top tier is not owed.

### Notes (advisory, no rework)

- The PR body says "the hint names every bit present". With record bits present, the hint always names both `viewAllRecords/modifyAllRecords`, whichever one is set, as it did before. Dropping an absent key does nothing, so this is wording only.
- `.changeset/36050-view-all-fields-bit.md` says "It is allowed on the `'*'` wildcard entry". That is true of the schema and of the built-in `organization_admin` set. A package-authored set is now refused by `security-wildcard-vama`, and that is stated only in this PR's lint changeset. Whoever next touches the 36050 changeset before release may want to qualify that sentence. It is not in this PR's file surface.

Not done by this record: approve, ready, auto-merge or queue.
